items.title: Abbey Lincoln — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Don't you think that Mr. Einstein was a scientist and an artist?

ctx.x: Of course. It comes through us because we're the human being and we practice the arts. We're made like this. I wrote a song called "Cage Bird." Birds sing

who are in cages just because they're made to do it. They're not inspired. They're caged and their lives are taken from them, but they sing. We're all given a sound here. All the animals. The human being is a world-builder. So, all praises are due to whatever made us. We're made like this. If you're loyal, if you put it first, it will put you first. Some people want money and some people like prestige. Whatever you're reaching for, it'll bring you a lot of things, but I don't think it comes to rescue people who…

It's interesting that you mentioned him because I had, in one of the questions I had written for you, it was quoting something Einstein once said to his daughter, which was that if she was ever feeling really bad, to look to nature.
